open_points.subject: OwnerFormField schema
open_points.text:
Facts: the field's name; whether it belongs to the request or to its values;
how its text is read.
open_points.question: What are the exact typed fields of OwnerFormField, including the closed domains of the destination and read-kind facts?
options: name: str, destination: request-or-values enum, read_kind: text-or-integer-or-boolean-or-enum enum
name plus explicit destination model/path and a typed parser or vocabulary reference
additional page/action, multiplicity, position, or allowed-values facts are fields too
open_points.default_guess: Use name, an explicit destination path, and a closed read-kind enum, adding a vocabulary reference for enumeration fields.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField destination
open_points.text: whether it belongs to the owner's request itself or to the values the owner gives
open_points.question: Does a row identify only the request/values root, or also the exact nested path and any tuple position where the parsed value is written?
options: Only a binary request-versus-values destination
An explicit full path within the selected destination
A full path plus a position for each positional or tuple component
open_points.default_guess: Restore a full destination path and positional marks where applicable.

witness.initial: The owner submits a form whose values contain nested or positional data.
events: The owner enters the field and submits the form.
The owner interface resolves its OwnerFormField row.
outcomes: The reader can identify only the values root and must guess the destination member.
The row identifies the exact nested member and positional component.
witness.observer: The generated owner-interface reader and the owner receiving the resulting change

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField name namespace
open_points.question: Is a field name globally unique across the whole owner interface, unique only within a page or action, or may one globally shared row be reused by several pages?
options: Names are globally unique and name alone selects a row
Identity is page/action plus name
Equal definitions may be shared across pages while differing definitions require page-scoped rows
open_points.default_guess: Make page/action plus field name select a row unless global uniqueness is stated and validated.

witness.initial: The create-project and record-customer pages both use a field named `name`.
events: The data provider adds the two owner pages to one release.
Each page's submission reader looks up `name`.
outcomes: A single global row is reused for both pages.
Two page-scoped rows represent distinct fields.
witness.observer: The data provider and the generated submission readers

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField table validity
open_points.question: What duplicate condition makes the owner form table invalid: repeated name, repeated page-and-name, repeated destination path, or only two completely equal rows?
options: No two rows may share a name
No two rows may share page/action and name
Duplicates are allowed when their other facts differ
Only completely duplicate rows are forbidden

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField population scope
open_points.text:
one field of the owner's pages — what the
owner types or picks in a form
open_points.question: Does the table contain only visible editable controls, or also query controls and submitted fields the owner does not type or pick, such as ids, revisions, confirmation values, request ids, and CSRF values?
options: Visible owner-entered or owner-selected form controls only
Every submitted form field, including hidden and generated controls
Form and query fields, but operational fields such as CSRF are handled outside this table
A separately enumerated subset for each owner action
open_points.default_guess: Include business request/value fields, visible or hidden, but handle authentication and CSRF outside this domain table; explicitly state whether query fields are included.

witness.initial: The owner has read a project card and opens its correction form with the current revision.
events: The page renders the revision without the owner typing it.
The owner changes the name and submits the form.
outcomes: The revision has an OwnerFormField row because the interface submits and reads it.
The revision is excluded because it is not something the owner types or picks and is read by separate code.
witness.observer: The generated correction action and its stale-revision tests

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField multiplicity
open_points.question: For repeated controls, tuples, or multi-valued inputs, is there one row for the logical field, one row for each occurrence or position, or is such input outside this model?
options: One row represents the whole repeated or multi-valued field
Each occurrence or tuple position has its own row
OwnerFormField supports scalar controls only
open_points.default_guess: Use one row per logical field with explicit cardinality or positional facts when the destination requires them.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField closed-list reading
open_points.text: as one of a closed list
open_points.question: Which fact identifies the particular closed list and the value produced from a selected member?
options: The row carries a reference to a declared enum or vocabulary
The destination field's type alone determines the closed list
The row embeds its allowed values
All closed-list fields share one list
open_points.default_guess: Have the row reference a declared enum or vocabulary; the later parsing algorithm may then use that fact.

witness.initial: One owner page selects a customer kind and another selects an object kind.
events: The owner selects a value on each page.
The interface reads both fields using rows whose read kind is merely `closed list`.
outcomes: The destination model type supplies two different lists implicitly.
Each row explicitly names the list it accepts.
witness.observer: The generated form renderer, reader, and validation tests

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField origin
open_points.text: The release: the owner form table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: Who creates OwnerFormField values, and from what authoritative input are they created: hand-authored provider data, declared owner-action contracts, page definitions, or generated model metadata?
options: The data provider authors the rows directly as release data
A release compiler derives them from owner-action contracts
The owner-interface pages register them
They are derived from request/value model metadata
open_points.default_guess: The data provider mints the immutable rows for each release from an explicitly declared owner-interface contract.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField product use
open_points.text:
as the owner interface names it on the page
and reads it back
open_points.question: Exactly which owner-interface actions read this table when rendering or accepting input, and can any product action create or change a row, or are rows replaced only by installing a new release?
options: Every owner-interface form render and submission reads it; no product action writes it
Only submission parsing reads it; rendering has a separate source
Only an enumerated subset of owner actions uses it
Product actions may register or alter rows at runtime
open_points.default_guess: The enumerated owner form renderers and submission readers both read it, no runtime product action creates or changes it, and a new release replaces the constant.
